newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FOCUS-Rural Press expands in U.S. market.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Rural Press expands in U.S. market.

text.p: Australian publisher Rural Press Ltd took a leading share of the U.S. agricultural publishing market on Monday, paying US$56.95 million for U.S. information provider Farm Progress Group.

The purchase complemented Rural Press's existing U.S. agricultural publishing business, and offered opportunities for growth in other areas, including database services and farm shows, said managing director Brian McCarthy.
"This now gives us the market leader position in the biggest agriculture market in the world," McCarthy told a media briefing.
Farm Progress, sold by ABC Inc, an indirect subsidiary of the Walt Disney Co, has 26 state farming titles, three national magazines, runs farm shows and operates an electronic data base.
McCarthy said he expected the group, which posted US$4.8 million in earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBIDTA) in calender 1996, to earn more than US$6.2 million in 1997.
This was due to the inclusion of a full year of a 1996 acquisition, and lower paper prices.

The decision to expand in the U.S. was based on a healthy outlook for the U.S. agriculture sector through to 2005, based on strong export opportunities, stable domestic demand and rising production, McCarthy said.
The agriculture print advertising market in the U.S. was also about A$208 million a year and expanding rapidly, compared with A$85 million in the Australian market.
"So we see a fair bit of upside in that U.S. market," he said.
Rural Press intended to keep the Farm Progress business intact and would look to its existing U.S. business for consolidation.
McCarthy said he hoped to lift margins from an 11.7 percent return on sales at present to nearer 15 percent within 12 months, but would keep existing management in place.
Rural press would also look to increase the number of paid for publications, currently only 30 percent of the total.
McCarthy said the acquisition would benefit Australian operations, allowing Rural Press to offer a greater range of U.S. agricultural news and the latest market prices through its Internet service.
Rural Press would continue to look for opportunities in Britain, Canada and South America and currently had A$30 million available for further acquisitions, he said.
